annotation.title_clean: Insights in the Social and Legal Perception of Robots and Users of Prostheses
annotation.title_en: Insights in the Social and Legal Perception of Robots and Users of Prostheses
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Mandl, S.; Bretschneider, M.; Meyer, S.; Gesmann-Nuissl, D.; Asbrock, F.; Meyer, B. et al.
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Two experimental studies examine how people perceive users of bionic prostheses and robots of varying anthropomorphism on Competence, Sociability and Morality, and, for robots, Legal Personality and Decision-Making Authority. Findings offer early insight into whether more anthropomorphic robots may need different legal treatment and inform design for acceptance as co-workers.
key_provisions_or_claims: Warmth in the Stereotype Content Model is split into Sociability and Morality.
Competence attributions to robots decrease with anthropomorphism.
Sociability, Morality, Legal Personality and Decision-Making Authority attributions vary with anthropomorphism.
Prosthesis users' perceived Competence and Morality vary with the technical sophistication of the prosthesis.
Public legal perceptions may bear on future legal treatment of anthropomorphic robots as co-workers.
